class.name: TerrainView
class.brief_description: Generates terrain on worker threads and publishes a finite preview across frames.
class.description: Captures the selected [RegionContainer] hierarchy into immutable C++ modifiers, then generates samples, indexed meshes and collision-face arrays on parallel section workers. A dedicated coordinator waits for the worker group; the main thread never performs sampling/meshing or waits for active generation during normal operation. Scene/render/physics-server registration necessarily remains on the main thread and is staged in small pieces across frames. The previous preview remains visible and collidable until the complete candidate is ready. Staging geometry is hidden and collision-disabled; errors/cancellation retain the previous preview. New accepted requests cancel obsolete work and coalesce to one latest pending snapshot. Node destruction cancels and joins outstanding workers for safe lifetime management. Runtime automatic generation remains disabled in the editor; explicit Inspector previews use the same asynchronous path. This node requires identity global transform and a threaded engine build. This is not production atomic physics-tick publication or incremental streaming.

method.name: cancel_generation
method.description: Requests cooperative cancellation without blocking the main loop and clears any pending replacement. The previous published preview remains. is_generating stays true until workers/staging have been discarded. Node destruction joins cancelled workers to prevent callbacks outliving their data.

method.name: generate_preview
method.description: Captures settings and queues worker generation. Returns true when accepted, not when finished. Listen for preview_generated, generation_failed or generation_cancelled, or poll is_generating. Authoring errors can return false immediately; worker budget/geometry failures arrive later through generation_failed. A new accepted request cancels obsolete work and replaces the one pending snapshot; only the latest accepted request can publish. Call from the main thread.

method.name: get_chunk_cells
method.description: Compatibility alias returning section_cells from the original prototype. World chunks now always span 16 metres.

method.name: get_progress
method.description: Returns active, stage, request_id, completed_sections, total_sections, published_pieces and total_pieces. Counts are a thread-safe progress snapshot. total_pieces is available only after workers finish.

method.name: get_statistics
method.description: Returns the last successful revision, request_id, bounds, chunk_count (16 metre spatial groups), chunk_size, section_count, section_cells, effective_spacing, column_samples, uniform_sections, mesh_sections, mesh_pieces, triangles and sample_payload_bytes. Includes source_triangles (before LOD), lod_sections (sections actually simplified), lod_enabled and lod_origin. Includes worker_limit (requested count capped by the pool), worker_threads_used and generation_on_main_thread for diagnostics. worker_ms is worker wall time; sampling_cpu_ms and meshing_cpu_ms sum elapsed durations of concurrent section callbacks, including scheduling/preemption; they are not OS CPU-time counters and may exceed worker wall time. Legacy sampling_ms/meshing_ms keys alias those CPU sums. layout_ms measures main-thread configuration capture; publication_ms accumulates main-thread registration elapsed time; commit_ms measures the final swap; max_publication_step_ms records the largest registration batch/commit. generation_ms includes queueing and frame scheduling. Legacy uniform_chunks/mesh_chunks refer to sections. Payload excludes meshes, collision, metadata and simultaneous old/staging previews. heightmap contains optional export path/request_id/column counts/spacing; heightmap_error reports a nonfatal diagnostic failure; heightmap_ms measures coordinator extraction/write time and is included in worker_ms, but not section CPU sums. Failed/cancelled jobs do not replace these statistics.

method.name: is_generating
method.description: Returns true while a worker, staged publication or pending replacement is active. Retiring hidden old scene nodes alone does not count as generation.

method.name: sample_field
method.description: Evaluates the last published immutable modifier snapshot at a world position. Negative values mean solid, positive values mean air, and zero marks the surface. This is the analytic generation field, not interpolation of the cached voxel array or a physics query. It can be evaluated outside the finite view request; container scopes still apply. Requires a successful generation and finite coordinates.

method.name: set_chunk_cells
method.description: Compatibility alias assigning section_cells for earlier scripts and saved scenes. World chunk size is fixed.

members.member: Optional absolute near-field mesh simplification error in metres, from zero to one. Zero preserves the unsimplified near mesh. Positive values target one quarter of source indices while retaining fixed boundary vertices and checking boundary topology. Error constraints may retain more triangles. Source samples and field evaluation remain unchanged; collision follows the resulting mesh. Requires lod_enabled.

Maximum distance simplification level, from one to four. Levels start at lod_distance and double their thresholds thereafter. Level N targets 1/4^N of source indices and uses lod_error multiplied by 2^(N-1). Fixed borders and geometric error may prevent reaching the target. Default two preserves earlier behavior.

Optional diagnostic CSV destination for the next generated candidate. Empty disables export. Use an absolute or user:// path. The worker coordinator extracts the highest air-to-solid crossing from completed cached samples before mesh LOD, with linear vertical interpolation. Hidden caves/overhangs are not represented. Files contain metadata and x,z,height,status rows; clipped-top/no-surface columns have no height. A temporary file is renamed after completion. Diagnostic failures are nonfatal to terrain and reported in statistics.heightmap_error. CSV metadata request_id identifies the candidate; a late cancellation during scene publication can retain a completed candidate CSV without publishing that preview. Await preview_generated and compare request IDs when coupling artifacts to a visible revision.

Diagnostic horizontal stride in source-lattice cells, from 1 to 32. Effective spacing is stride times the prepared cache spacing. The export uses lattice points inside the exact requested bounds and scans at original vertical spacing. This does not change terrain generation or meshing resolution.

Enable worker-side mesh simplification by distance from lod_origin. Requires the meshoptimizer module; otherwise the request fails explicitly. Sampling remains full resolution. Collision uses the resulting mesh and is approximate in simplified sections. Captured per generation request; does not change existing previews continuously.
World-space player or camera-focus position used for LOD. Distance is measured to the nearest point of each section box in 3D.

Full-detail distance in metres. Sections beyond it target one quarter of source triangles, and beyond twice it target one sixteenth. Boundary locking and error limits may prevent reaching those targets. Minimum 4 metres.

Maximum simplifier absolute geometric error in metres for the first reduced level; twice this for the second. Range 0.01 to 2. Topological borders remain fixed to preserve section seams. This is the simplifier error metric, not an exact signed-field or collision tolerance.

Queues one preview generation when the scene starts running. Automatic generation is disabled in editor mode; the Generate Preview Inspector action remains available for an explicit editor preview. Property changes do not continuously rebuild terrain.
Prepare collision-face arrays on workers and register static concave triangle shapes during staged main-thread publication. Disable for rendering-only view-distance experiments. Captured per request.
Inspector action that calls [method generate_preview]. This editor-only callable is not saved in the scene.
Finite world-space request box, intersected with the bounded root area. Mesh triangles are clipped to this exact box without adding artificial edge walls.

Soft per-frame main-thread registration budget, from 1 to 16 ms, default 4. Geometry is split into pieces of at most 1024 triangles by workers. A single scene/server operation and the final visibility/collision swap cannot be preempted and may exceed the budget. Hidden old nodes retire separately under a small cleanup budget.
Path to the top [RegionContainer] for this view.

Maximum candidate lattice samples including section halos, from 1000000 to 64000000; default 16000000. Requests also have a 16384-section limit. Exceeding either fails asynchronously before dense arrays are allocated, retaining the previous preview. This is not a total process-memory limit.

Requested experimental grid spacing in metres, accepted from 0.025 to 2. The generated lattice is snapped to fit whole sections inside fixed 16 metre world chunks, at the requested spacing or finer. Read effective_spacing from statistics for the actual value. Smaller values increase cost and may exceed the preview budget. A chosen spacing does not guarantee preservation of every feature of that size.

Preferred cells per internal section edge, from 4 to 64. Generation chooses a nearby divisor of the 16 metre world chunk lattice; actual values are reported in statistics. Dense sections include border samples plus a one-sample gradient halo on both sides (actual cells + 3 samples per edge). World chunk dimensions never change. The old serialized chunk_cells property is retained as a compatibility alias.
Description of the latest success or failure. Inspect this after a failed generation; [method get_statistics] still describes the previous successful result.
Maximum generated triangles, from 10000 to 4000000; default 2000000. Workers cancel the candidate if aggregate section output exceeds this budget; no partial candidate is published.

Requested maximum parallel section tasks, at least 1. Defaults to the logical processor count reported by the operating system. Actual usage is limited by available worker-pool threads, work size and shared pool scheduling. Terrain group tasks use the full worker queue rather than the smaller low-priority allocation. Explicit project worker-pool limits remain honoured. A dedicated waiting coordinator is additional. One worker still keeps generation off the main thread. Captured per request.

signal.name: generation_cancelled
signal.description: Emitted when explicit cancellation is requested while work is active. Worker cleanup may still be in progress; poll is_generating to observe completion.

signal.name: generation_failed
signal.description: Emitted on the main thread for immediate authoring errors or later worker budget/geometry failures. The previous successful preview/statistics remain available.

signal.name: generation_started
signal.description: Emitted on the main thread when a request snapshot is accepted. Its ID also appears in progress and successful statistics.

signal.name: preview_generated
signal.description: Emitted on the main thread after a complete candidate becomes visible/collidable and its data/statistics are published. Cancelled or superseded jobs never emit success.
